links.outcome: Sensitivity loss when sECGs the algorithm classified as false are ignored, versus a three-physician board
links.effect: Estimated loss of sensitivity was 2.6% on a 2000-sECG sample. Most falsely rejected true arrhythmias had the same arrhythmia type classified as true before or within 3 days. 42.8% of sECGs were filtered as false.
links.quote: The loss of sensitivity is estimated as 2.6%.

unlisted_practices: Using AI to filter false-positive ECG detections from implantable cardiac monitors to reduce remote review workload

screen.reason: Evaluates the workflow workload reduction and clinical sensitivity impact of implementing an AI-based filter (SmartECG) on remote cardiac monitoring alerts compared to standard unmitigated review.

primary.practice: AI-based false alert filtering to reduce clinician review burden
